justification: HFM is a learned policy deciding when the agent must defer to a human expert rather than proceed unaided, i.e. an escalation gate; evidence is lab Minecraft task-success runs, not a deployed setting.

Object is intrinsic self-correction and whether structured reflection feedback helps; it does not, yielding the 'structure snowballing' account. Evidence is a lab comparison on Qwen3-8B with and without constrained decoding.

Tested mechanism is recursive refinement: self-criticism, adversarial stress-testing and integrating critical feedback. A designed simple-vs-structured pipeline comparison over nine cases in the lab, no deployment.

CR-Planner iteratively selects and executes sub-goals under critic-model rewards, so the contribution is what the loop does next; validated on competitive programming, math and retrieval benchmarks in the lab.

CMRF's claim is Adaptive Iterative Refinement: step-by-step inferences are self-corrected via a coherence module across rounds. Lab benchmark results on VCR, A-OKVQA and DailyLife-MRC, no real deployment.

IoT's Inner Dialogue Agent generates critiques as prompts that the LLM agent uses to rewrite its answer each round, i.e. revise-on-feedback; validated on GPQA, Game of 24, Crosswords and HotpotQA in the lab.

Ablations credit iterative verification by the verifier agent, checking constraints and blocking error propagation, over the multi-agent framing; evidence is accuracy on the authors' PRIME-Bench, a lab benchmark.
The contribution is the refinement step: a VLM critic's feedback drives sequential corrections of the generated image; measured on ConceptMix, T2I-CompBench and Visual Jenga, a lab benchmark study.
IdealGPT iteratively decomposes the query into sub-questions that fix the next step of the divide-and-conquer loop; zero-shot benchmark results on VCR and SNLI-VE, prototype only.

The studied object is whether iterative LLM refinement helps: 40 rounds of 'improvement' degrade security. A controlled lab experiment over 400 generated samples and four prompting strategies, not field data.

The novelty is how the judgement is produced: ILP-learned relation rules act as an online step-level verifier that diagnoses violations before repair; validated on the CLUTRR benchmark across five models.

Adaptive-Consistency keeps self-consistency sampling intact and only changes how many samples are drawn, via a lightweight stopping criterion; validated on 17 existing reasoning and coding datasets with three LLMs.

CRAFT turns the prompt into explicit dependency-structured constraints that a VLM verifies, and only violated constraints release an update; runner-up critique_and_revision. Lab benchmark gains across model families.

Contributes a probabilistic-programming formalism for composing repeated model calls with control flow and dynamic structure, a new way of looking at the field, demonstrated by re-expressing scratchpads, verifiers and STaR.
PiVe's contribution is the trained verifier module that judges LLM graph output and issues fine-grained corrective instructions; validated on three existing graph datasets in the lab.

AVA's loop has the agent perceive its own rendered visualization and iterate on the result toward the user's stated goal; the paper offers a design framework with usage scenarios and proof-of-concept agents only.
GenPRM is a process reward model that reasons and runs code verification to judge each reasoning step, i.e. the acceptance criterion itself; validated on ProcessBench and math benchmarks in the lab.
T1 is a two-stage verification scheme: external tools filter candidates before a small LM gives the final verdict, so the contribution is how the check is produced; validated on the MATH benchmark.
CGR probes answer certainty to halt reasoning early against a thinking budget, a stopping and allocation rule; validated on AIME2025 over 64 seeds in the lab.

Negative early exit and adaptive boosting reallocate compute among concurrent MCTS searches for p99 latency while accuracy holds; runner-up deliberative_search for the pruning. Lab measurements on a vLLM integration.
DCR's primitive is divergent generation of candidate solutions followed by convergent reconciliation that selects among them, changing the exploration shape; validated on AIME 2024/2025 in the lab.

The contribution is a compute-optimal policy allocating test-time compute per prompt by difficulty, leaving the search methods themselves intact; a lab study of scaling behaviour on math prompts against best-of-N.

TAB is a GRPO-trained policy allocating token budgets across turns under a global constraint, i.e. how much the loop gets; validated on agentic benchmarks against static and off-the-shelf budget baselines.

Studies verification-cost-limited reasoning and allocates verifier calls adaptively across states rather than changing candidate generation; validated on MATH with 44% fewer verifier calls than best-of-N and beam search.

The claim is that verifier-based signal is what makes test-time scaling work, versus verifier-free trace cloning; a proof plus a compute-matched lab comparison on didactic and math problems with 3/8/32B models.
